subject: Embeddings model fit validation & next steps
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmeadvisors.com>

Cc: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: embeddings needs & validation questions

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — super helpful. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move to a short eval: 

Scope: semantic search over product docs and help articles (~1.2M docs, average length ~250 tokens). We also plan to add user-generated support tickets (~600k) later this year.
Current setup: using openai-embedding-ada-002 (768d), vector index in Pinecone, cosine similarity.
Primary goals: improve recall for long-tail queries, reduce false-positive semantic matches, and keep inference cost predictable. Also concerned about embedding drift as content updates daily.

Immediate asks:
- Recommended models/configs to try (dimensionality tradeoffs, latency expectations).
- Example benchmark results (recall@10, MRR, NDCG) vs our baseline.
- Suggested prompt/embedding pre-processing (stopword handling, chunking, pooling).
- Any red flags re: regression risk if we move to larger dims or quantized variants.

Attached is a small sample of 1k queries + truth labels we pulled for a quick evaluation (we'll upload the full 10k if helpful). Happy to share access to our index if you want Redwood to run the sweep.

Next step: Could you share a short plan for a 1k-10k evaluation and a recommended model shortlist? Also propose a time for a 30-min follow-up next week.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Data Science, Ava Digital
[Attachment: sample-1k-queries.csv (CSV, 120 KB)]

From: marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings needs & validation questions

Hi Jane — great talking earlier. TL;DR: recommend a quick 1k eval with two model families (1024d and 768d) + monitoring plan; see attached baseline report and prompt set.

Summary / recommendation:
- Models to try: redwood-emb-v1-large (1024d) — higher recall, slightly higher latency/cost; open-embed-3-small (768d) — lower cost, faster, sometimes similar precision on short queries.
- Quantized variants: try int8 or float16 for inference testing, but validate quality — we sometimes see small MRR drops with aggressive quantization on long-tail queries.
- Dimensionality tradeoff: 1024d improved recall@10 by ~6 points versus 768d on our internal legal-docs benchmark; expect similar gains for long-tail product queries but test on your sample.

Proposed 1k evaluation plan (can execute remotely):
1) Run embeddings for the 1k query set on three variants: baseline (openai-ada-002 768d), redwood-emb-v1-large (1024d), open-embed-3-small (768d).
2) Re-index top-k (k=100) and compute recall@10, MRR, NDCG@10, and average cosine distance to positives.
3) Check stability across query types (short vs long) and compute distribution of cosine similarities for positives vs negatives.
4) Quick sensitivity: downsample index to simulate drift and measure drop in recall.

Attached: embeddings-eval-summary.csv (baseline numbers we computed on a similar retail dataset) and prompt-sets-v1.csv (recommended chunking / stopword rules). Also shared a Drive folder with full eval harness and scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcExample

Preliminary baseline numbers (example):
- openai-ada-002 (768d): recall@10 = 0.68, MRR = 0.41, NDCG@10 = 0.63
- redwood-emb-v1-large (1024d): recall@10 = 0.74, MRR = 0.49, NDCG@10 = 0.69
- open-embed-3-small (768d): recall@10 = 0.70, MRR = 0.44, NDCG@10 = 0.65

Notes on drift & monitoring:
- For daily-updating content, we recommend embedding-drift detectors (monitor distribution of average cosine to a stable set of anchor docs) and weekly reindexing for hot content.
- Set regression alert thresholds: MRR drop > 5% absolute or recall@10 drop > 4% triggers investigation.

Next steps:
- If you grant access to the 1k sample and a temporary read-only index endpoint, we can run the full sweep in 48 hours and share a report.
- Alternatively, we can share a small runner you can run in your environment — whichever you prefer.

Scheduling: I have availability Mon/Tue next week 10-12 PT or Wed 2-4 PT.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings needs & validation questions

Hi Jane — quick note on quality/regression concerns (looping Marcus + Rishi):

We recently saw a subtle regression when moving a customer from a 768->512-d quantized variant: overall recall held but MRR for long-form queries dropped ~6 points. Root cause was compression of informative dimensions used by long queries.

Recommendations:
- Start with an A/B evaluation (50/50 traffic) for the 1k seed before committing index-wide, validate per-query-type MRR and top1 precision.
- If you try quantized variants, keep one unquantized (or less-aggressive quant) baseline for comparison.
- Monitoring: daily jobs that compute embedding centroid shifts for new content batches and per-query cosine distribution. We can provide a small thresholding script.

Operational suggestions:
- Reindex cadence: nightly for help articles with high edit rates; weekly for product docs.
- Dimensionality: prefer 1024d for recall-sensitive workloads where cost permits; consider 768d for read-heavy, cost-sensitive scenarios.

I've added two quick items in the Drive folder (a short script to compute centroid drift + a suggested dashboard template).

Happy to review the 1k results and define rollout policy.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior ML Ops, Redwood Inference
